result.summary: Adds a `getMemoryLoad()` method to the IPC mining interface to estimate the memory footprint of block templates held by external clients. `BlockTemplateManager` tracks active templates via weak references and calculates aggregate memory usage from template data structures plus referenced transactions that are no longer present in the mempool. It also changes `BlockTemplateManager` storage in `NodeContext` to `std::shared_ptr` so asynchronous IPC template cleanup can finish safely after node shutdown begins.
result.problem: External mining clients (such as Stratum v2 template providers) can hold block templates indefinitely over IPC. Because templates hold `CTransactionRef` references, transactions removed or evicted from the mempool remain pinned in node memory without any visibility for clients to inspect or manage that memory burden.
evidence: PR description: 'IPC clients can hold block templates indefinitely, keeping transactions alive after they leave the mempool. This adds getMemoryLoad() to estimate the memory held on behalf of all mining clients, as discussed in bitcoin/bitcoin#33899.'
PR description links client-side integration in stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63 to prune stale templates based on memory load.
result.changed_since_previous: No structural changes to the interface or memory accounting approach; rebased with minor refactoring and test updates.
result.card: Adds a getMemoryLoad() method to the IPC mining interface to report the memory footprint of active block templates held by external clients. BlockTemplateManager tracks templates via weak pointers and estimates memory consumed by their internal structures along with transactions they pin that are no longer in the mempool. This enables external clients such as Stratum v2 template providers to monitor memory pressure and destroy stale templates, resolving tracking concerns discussed in issue #33899.

risk.why: A synchronization mistake or lifetime issue between the IPC template wrapper and BlockTemplateManager could cause deadlocks or use-after-free crashes during node shutdown.
